summary: AstroVitals is a personalized health-monitoring prototype designed to support astronaut well-being during long-duration space missions. It generates simulated health records for five astronaut profiles over 180 days and establishes individual health baselines to identify unusual changes over time. By combining direction-aware robust Z-score analysis using median and MAD with an Isolation Forest machine learning model, the system identifies potential anomalies and presents explainable alerts with suggested next steps. It also provides locally stored mood check-ins using SQLite. Unlike generic monitoring systems, AstroVitals considers individual health patterns and gradual mission-related changes rather than relying solely on fixed thresholds. The prototype demonstrates how personalized anomaly detection can support astronaut health awareness and proactive monitoring in isolated space environments.
details:
AstroVitals is a personalized astronaut health-monitoring prototype developed to demonstrate how anomaly detection can support health awareness during long-duration space missions.

How it works

The application generates a synthetic dataset representing five astronaut profiles across 180 mission days. For each astronaut, the first 30 days establish an individual health baseline. It then uses a rolling 30-day personal norm to account for gradual changes and reduce false alerts caused by normal mission drift.

Anomaly detection

AstroVitals combines two complementary approaches:

  1. Direction-aware robust Z-score analysis using the median and Median Absolute Deviation (MAD) to identify unusual deviations in health indicators.
  2. An Isolation Forest machine learning model to identify potentially anomalous patterns across multiple indicators.

The system displays explainable anomaly alerts and suggested next steps. It also supports local mood check-ins, stored in an SQLite database.

Health indicators demonstrated

The simulated records include heart rate, sleep, activity, mood, stress, radiation index, bone index and muscle index.

Technology stack

  • Programming language: Python
  • Backend: Flask
  • Data processing: Pandas and NumPy
  • Machine learning: Scikit-learn
  • Database: SQLite
  • Frontend: HTML and CSS

Innovation and impact

The key innovation is personalized anomaly detection rather than relying exclusively on generic fixed thresholds. Individual baselines and rolling personal norms help demonstrate how monitoring systems could account for differences between astronauts and gradual changes during long missions.

AstroVitals runs locally without requiring a cloud account or external API, making it suitable as a lightweight research prototype.

Scientific limitations

All generated health records and injected anomalies are synthetic demonstration data. They are not actual astronaut medical records, measured radiation exposure or clinically validated health thresholds. AstroVitals is not a medical device and does not diagnose or predict clinical events. Real-world deployment would require validated sensors, clinical review, security controls and operational approval.
